card.title: Hooke's law and Young modulus — stress over strain

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Stress (force per area) produces strain (fractional deformation); within the elastic limit their ratio is a material constant — the modulus. Young modulus stretches wires, bulk modulus squeezes volumes, shear modulus skews shapes. Poisson's ratio couples stretch to thinning. The stretched wire stores the work as elastic potential energy.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Hooke: F = −kx  ·  Young Y = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) = stress/strain (Pa)  ·  bulk B = −(ΔP)/(ΔV/V)  ·  shear η = (F/A)/θ  ·  Poisson σ = −(lateral strain)/(longitudinal strain)  ·  U = ½·stress·strain·volume = ½kx²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Hooke's law holds only within the ELASTIC limit — past yield, permanent set begins and the ratio collapses. Moduli assume small, uniform, isothermal deformation of a homogeneous sample. Poisson's ratio for most metals sits near 0.3 (theoretical ceiling 0.5).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Rubber stretches far but with a non-linear curve (elastic, not Hookean). Steel wire under 100 N on 2 mm²: stress = F/A = 100/(2×10⁻⁶) = 5×10⁷ Pa (NEB 2022). Breaking stress ends the story at fracture; ductile vs brittle is decided by how far plastic flow runs first.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Steel wire, A = 2 mm² = 2×10⁻⁶ m², F = 100 N → stress = 100/(2×10⁻⁶) = 5×10⁷ Pa. With Y = 2×10¹¹ Pa, strain = stress/Y = 2.5×10⁻⁴ — a 1 m wire stretches just 0.25 mm, which is why the modulus earns its 'stiffness' name (NEB 2022, 3 marks).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Moduli are bulk averages — defects, temperature and loading rate shift them. Hooke says nothing past yield: creep, fatigue and hysteresis live outside it. The U = ½kx² form counts only recoverable energy; plastic work is dissipated, not stored.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Energy in a stretched wire: dW = F·dx with F = (YA/L)x → W = ∫₀^ΔL (YA/L)x·dx = ½·(YA/L)(ΔL)² = ½·(F/A)(ΔL/L)·(AL) = ½·stress·strain·volume. Energy density is the area under the stress–strain curve — triangle while Hooke holds.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Modulus = stress/strain, always in Pa — if units mismatch, the answer is wrong. Y problems: write F/A over ΔL/L and solve the fraction ladder. 'Define + SI units' of stress, strain, Y is a guaranteed 2–3 marker (NEB 2023 asked exactly this).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): define stress, strain, Young's modulus + SI units. NEB 2023 (2): Y formula + unit. NEB 2022 (3): 100 N on 2 mm² steel wire — stress, then strain with Y = 2×10¹¹ Pa.
